review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it uses (`realSpectrum`, `restrictedSpectrum` in AbstractSpectrum.lean). I also read the neighbouring file BoundedOffDiagonalRestrictionSpectrum.lean and grepped for how membership in `realSpectrum` is handled elsewhere. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes, so the only simp-interface issue I found is a missing canonical membership lemma for `realSpectrum`. The unrelated lemma `TauCeti.LinearPMap.mem_realSpectrum_iff` is for the unbounded `LinearPMap` version, so it does not cover the bounded `DavisKahan.Foundation.realSpectrum`. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether adding the simp lemma would interact with other simp sets, so the proposal is untested. The `Set.mem_ofPred_eq` / `Set.mem_setOf_eq` step in the existing `simp only` calls may or may not still be needed after the change. I also did not review the second theorem's `restrictedSpectrum` handling in detail, because its rewrite goes through an explicit equality lemma and does not use simp.

findings.problem: `DavisKahan.Foundation.realSpectrum` is a plain `def`, `{r | (r : 𝕜) ∈ spectrum 𝕜 A}`. It has no membership-unfolding lemma, simp or otherwise. To use or prove `lam ∈ realSpectrum T`, the proof has to reach for `change ... ∈ spectrum ℂ T`, which depends on definitional unfolding. Other files do the same, for example `change (r : ℂ) ∈ spectrum ℂ T at hr` in `realSpectrum_bddAbove` and `realSpectrum_bddBelow`, and `simp only [realSpectrum, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, ...]` in AbstractSpectrum.lean and Complexification/SubmoduleEquiv.lean. `simp` will not unfold the def by itself, so `r ∈ realSpectrum A` is not normalised to `(r : 𝕜) ∈ spectrum 𝕜 A`, and each caller has to find its own `change` or unfolding recipe. The bounded-operator namespace has no counterpart to `TauCeti.LinearPMap.mem_realSpectrum_iff`, which is `@[simp]` for the unbounded version.
findings.proposed_change: In AbstractSpectrum.lean, right after `def realSpectrum`, add `@[simp] theorem mem_realSpectrum_iff {A : E →L[𝕜] E} {r : ℝ} : r ∈ realSpectrum A ↔ (r : 𝕜) ∈ spectrum 𝕜 A := Iff.rfl`. This rewrites toward the Mathlib `spectrum` form, which already has simp and API support. The right-hand side contains no `realSpectrum`, so it cannot loop. Because the name is in the `DavisKahan.Foundation` namespace, it will not clash with `TauCeti.LinearPMap.mem_realSpectrum_iff`. Then replace `change (lam : ℂ) ∈ spectrum ℂ T; exact hz` here with `exact (mem_realSpectrum_iff).2 hz`, or `simpa using hz`. Replace the `change ... at hr` lines in `realSpectrum_bddAbove`/`realSpectrum_bddBelow` with `rw [mem_realSpectrum_iff] at hr` or `simp at hr`.
findings.benefit: Membership in the bounded real spectrum gets one canonical, discoverable normal form. Proofs here and in the neighbouring files (`realSpectrum_bddAbove`/`realSpectrum_bddBelow`, `BoundedOffDiagonalOrderedGap`, `restrictedSpectrum_top`) no longer rely on definitional `change` or hand-written `simp only [realSpectrum, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, ...]` lists. It also matches the unbounded `LinearPMap` interface.

evidence.excerpt:
def realSpectrum (A : E →L[𝕜] E) : Set ℝ :=
  {r | (r : 𝕜) ∈ spectrum 𝕜 A}
change (r : ℂ) ∈ spectrum ℂ T at hr
